tier_reason: The only number is a single cold Yeppp.jl @elapsed line from 2018, and Dispatch.cpp matches exact CPU models only, so every CPU after Haswell (and all AMD after Piledriver) runs the scalar C fallback; the binding's own issues #37 and #32 measure Yeppp slower than Base on such CPUs. Directional at best, and only for CPUs up to Haswell.

corrections.caveats: Vectorized paths dispatch on exact CPU model (Dispatch.cpp): Broadwell/Skylake and later, Excavator and Zen fall back to scalar C, so Yeppp.jl #37 (0.66x of Base) and #32 (i7-6820HQ slower than a loop) contradict the README's 3x line (single cold run, 2018). yepBuiltin_Log_64f_64f returns 710.188 for NaN (issue #31) and 709.78 for +Inf. Mirror lacks generated yepCore/yepMath sources; binaries gone.

tier_reason: The only concrete comparison reachable (RetriEval, FAISS 1.12.0 on Xeon 6) builds FAISS via faiss-sys with no FAISS_OPT_LEVEL, so the baseline ran a generic target without AVX2/F16C/AVX-512 while USearch used runtime dispatch (crippled-baseline precedent); the first-party README table's setup is unverifiable (blog blocked). Directional only.

corrections.caveats: RetriEval numbers compare USearch with NumKong runtime dispatch against FAISS built at the generic target (faiss-sys build.rs, no FAISS_OPT_LEVEL): FAISS SQfp16/SQbf16 adds 2,545/3,800 per s vs its own f32 7,491 per s, so the 2.8-4.3x half-precision leads are against a crippled baseline. First-party README table setup unverifiable (unum.cloud blocked). Open #735 concurrent add() leaves nodes unreachable; deadlocks #396, #354.

tier_reason: Independent benchm-ml numbers stay tier B; the R gbm row is not like for like (interaction.depth counts splits, not depth) and the scikit-learn rows compare 1 dense thread against 32 sparse threads.

corrections.caveats: benchm-ml (szilard) is independent but not like for like: xgboost used all 32 cores while R gbm is single-threaded and its interaction.depth=16 means 16 splits per tree, not depth 16 (gbm tree.cpp); scikit-learn ratios exclude encoding and compare a dense exact split on 1 thread with a sparse scan on 32 threads; H2O beat xgboost at 10M rows in the same table (3500 vs 9000 s, 300 vs 1000 s). Measured version used the exact updater (hist arrived in v0.7).
